speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help me narrow this down, have these symptoms been constant or do they come and go in spells? Also, do you feel any ringing in your ears or have you noticed any recent head injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) is less likely given the constant nature of the symptoms; the clinical picture of sustained vertigo with nausea in a young male is most suggestive of Vestibular Neuritis or Labyrinthitis, though Meniere's disease remains a differential. REQUEST TEST: Audiometry to rule out sensorineural hearing loss and assess vestibular function.
